final.title: Spot vendor price changes before they hit cash flow
final.body:
If you run a small business, vendor pricing changes are easy to miss until the invoice arrives. The real workflow decision is simple: are you checking for changes early, or are you finding them late and then doing the math by hand?

This is a good fit only when the information already comes in digital text form, such as email, a portal export, or a structured invoice. It is not a fit for scan-heavy paperwork, and OCR/PDF scan ingestion is not part of our current scope. If prices rarely change, manual spot-checks may be enough. No need to build a robot for a once-a-quarter shrug.

The control should stay with you. A small detection step can flag when a rate or amount moves beyond your chosen baseline, but the owner still decides what happens next: accept it, question it, or renegotiate. Payment or contract changes should not happen without human approval.

If you want to test whether this is worth automating, ask three questions: how often do key vendors send pricing updates, in what format do they arrive, and do you already keep a baseline of expected rates? If the answer is unclear, start there. That tells you whether this is a repeatable workflow worth automating or just another spreadsheet wearing a cape.
